# Test Fixtures

Test archives used to verify cooViewer archive handling, image ordering,
filename decoding, image dimensions, scaling, and rendering.

## Source images

The canonical source images are stored in `src/`.

All images are released under CC0 1.0 Universal.

## Generate archives

```sh
tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.sh
```

Generated archives are written to `generated/` and are not committed to Git.

The script generates fixtures for:

- ZIP
- CBZ
- TAR
- 7z, when `7zz` is installed
- CBR (non-solid and solid), when `rar` is installed
- ZIP with UTF-8 Japanese filenames
- ZIP with CP932 Japanese filenames

## Filename encoding fixtures

`test_utf8.zip` stores Japanese filenames as UTF-8 and sets the ZIP UTF-8
language encoding flag.

`test_sjis.zip` stores Japanese filenames as CP932 byte sequences without
the ZIP UTF-8 language encoding flag. This represents legacy ZIP archives
commonly created by Japanese Windows applications.

The exact filename encoding is part of the fixture and is generated by
`make_sjis_fixture.py`.

`test_solid.cbr` is a solid RAR archive (`rar a -s`); RAR's solid
compression may reorder entries by file type for a better ratio, so
this fixture's archive order does not match `test.cbr`'s — see
`docs/tasks/2026-07-14-02-rar-partial-lazy.md` for why that matters
to the RAR reader.

## Committed RAR5 final-block fixture

`sample/header_error_sample.rar` is a valid RAR5 archive containing one
synthetic binary payload. It has a non-final compressed block that produces
the complete payload followed by a final compressed block that produces no
output. With the currently vendored libarchive, a partially filled final
`archive_read_data()` request returns the complete payload and the following
request reports a block-header error.

The fixture contains no user data or third-party media. It is committed so the
archive engine suite can verify the strict size-and-CRC recovery path now and
the normal EOF path after a future libarchive update fixes the decoder state.
See [libarchive issue #3352](https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/issues/3352)
and [pull request #3361](https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/pull/3361).

## Expected page order

1. `001.png`
2. `002.jpg`
3. `003.png`
4. `004.jpg`

Japanese filename fixtures use the following names:

1. `001_表紙.png`
2. `002_縦長表示.jpg`
3. `003_網点とカケアミ.png`
4. `004_拡大縮小.jpg`

## Baseline results — 2026-07-11

Manual check of every archive in `generated/` against the current
Deployment build (v1.3.6 + resource consolidation, commit `ded598e`),
opened in the app; page names/order read from the page-bar HUD.

| Archive | Opens | Filenames correct | Page order correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| test.zip | ✓ | ✓ (001.png–004.jpg) | ✓ (1→2/3 spread→4) |
| test.cbz | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| test.tar | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| test.7z | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| test.cbr | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| test_utf8.zip | ✓ | ✓ UTF-8 Japanese decoded | ✓ |
| test_utf8.7z | ✓ | ✓ UTF-8 Japanese decoded | ✓ (pages 1–3 verified) |
| test_utf8.cbr | ✓ | ✓ UTF-8 Japanese decoded | ✓ |
| test_sjis.zip | ✓ | ✓ CP932 detected & decoded | ✓ |

CP932/UTF-8 filename decoding is performed inside XADMaster via
UniversalDetector — relevant baseline for any future submodule swap
(see `docs/audit-20260711.md` §2b).

## Encrypted ZIP fixtures

`tests/engine/run_encryption_test.sh` verifies that the vendored libzip can
decrypt password-protected ZIP archives (see
`docs/DECISIONS.md` — libzip + CommonCrypto). It generates its fixtures at
run time into `tests/fixtures/generated/` (not committed):

- `enc_aes.zip` — WinZip **AES-256**, created by the test via libzip.
- `enc_trad.zip` — traditional **PKWARE ZipCrypto**, created by the test via
  libzip.
- `enc_trad_cli.zip` — traditional ZipCrypto created independently by the
  system `zip -e` tool, to check cross-tool decryption.

Each contains a single entry `secret.txt` whose contents are a deterministic
synthetic byte pattern (`(i*37+11) & 0xff` for `i` in 0..511) — not an image
and not a copyrighted asset, so no additional licensing applies. The test
password is `cooViewer-secret-42`. These fixtures exercise the vendored
library only; no application code handles encrypted archives yet.
